title: Audit and update browser-window docs to match v1.4.6 attribute surface
description:
## Why
v1.4.6 added iframe permissions passthrough (allow / allowfullscreen / referrerpolicy) but documentation hasn't been updated. Spot-check shows:

- README.md (which becomes the npm package page) does not mention the new attrs
- docs/api.html likely missing the new attrs as well
- Possibly other gaps from prior versions — full audit needed

The v1.4.6 npm publish will go out without README updates unless we ship a follow-up patch.

## What to do
1. Build the canonical attribute list from src/browser-window.js — both @attr JSDoc (lines 7-18) and observedAttributes (lines 314-327). These should match. Cross-check against custom-elements.json too.
2. Audit each of these surfaces and produce a gap list:
   - README.md (becomes the npm landing page)
   - docs/api.html (the API reference page on the docs site)
   - docs/index.html (homepage usage examples)
   - docs/demos.html (demo coverage — does any demo show the new attrs?)
   - browser-window.d.ts (TypeScript declarations)
3. Fix all gaps so the surface is documented consistently across:
   - Source JSDoc (truth)
   - observedAttributes (truth)
   - custom-elements.json (manifest)
   - README (npm)
   - docs site (api.html especially)
   - .d.ts (TypeScript users)
4. Add a usage example for the `allow` attribute showing the Chrome built-in AI / Gemini Nano case (this was the motivating use case from vanilla-breeze).
5. After docs land, publish a doc-only patch (1.4.7) so npm picks up the new README.

## Acceptance
- Every attribute in observedAttributes appears in: README, docs/api.html, browser-window.d.ts
- README has a usage example for `allow=`
- npm package page (after publish) shows the new attrs
acceptance_criteria: Every attr in observedAttributes is documented in README.md, docs/api.html, and browser-window.d.ts. README includes an  usage example. v1.4.7 published with updated README.
